one_liner: PostgreSQL's own Bison parser as a standalone C library; raw parse about 5-7x faster than sqlparser-rs in a rival's harness.
what_it_does: Compiles the real PostgreSQL server parser (scan.l lexer, gram.y Bison grammar, node types, memory contexts) into libpg_query.a so programs outside the server can parse SQL and PL/pgSQL. The public C API returns the parse tree as JSON (pg_query_parse) or Protobuf (pg_query_parse_protobuf) and adds fingerprinting, normalization, statement splitting, token scanning, deparsing and a summary call; every result struct is freed with a matching pg_query_free_* function. It is not a drop-in for sqlparser-rs or any generic SQL parser: it accepts exactly one PostgreSQL major version's grammar and nothing else.
how_it_is_fast: The speed is PostgreSQL's: a table-driven LALR(1) Bison parser fed by a Flex scanner, allocating nodes in a per-call AllocSet memory context that is deleted wholesale at the end, built at -O3 by default. The raw tree (List of RawStmt nodes) is cheap; most of the public-API cost is the JSON or Protobuf serialization on top, which in the ParserSQL harness takes the simple SELECT from 684 ns raw to 1,872 ns with JSON. The 18.1.0 release replaced protobuf-c with the vendored upb runtime, which the changelog says is substantially faster (no numbers published).
when_to_use: Tools that must accept exactly what a given PostgreSQL major version accepts: linters, query analyzers, migration checkers, language servers, proxies and query-fingerprinting pipelines.
Grouping or deduplicating queries by fingerprint compatible with Postgres queryid semantics (Postgres 18 rules by default, PG17 compatibility flag available).
Bindings from Ruby, Go, Rust, Python, Node or OCaml where a mature wrapper already exists (pg_query, pg_query_go, pg_query.rs, pglast and others).
Single-statement parse latency in the sub-microsecond to few-microsecond range is acceptable (about 0.2-3.3 us raw, 0.4-8.7 us with JSON on a Ryzen 9 5950X in the ParserSQL harness).
when_not_to_use: Any dialect other than PostgreSQL (MySQL, SQLite, T-SQL, BigQuery): the grammar rejects it; sqlparser-rs or a dialect-aware parser is the tool.

Hot paths that need the fastest possible PostgreSQL parse: the raw tree is only reachable through the internal header pg_query_internal.h, and the public JSON path costs about 2.7x the raw parse; in the same harness the hand-written ParserSQL was about 3x faster than the raw path.
Builds that cannot afford a large C library: the static archive is about 30 MB per the ParserSQL instructions and the README warns that make takes up to 3 minutes.
Normalizing untrusted query text on releases older than 18.1.0 or 17-6.2.4: GHSA-6ggm-xmc9-8ffg is a heap out-of-bounds write and read in pg_query_normalize.

Projects that need one parser across Postgres major versions: each major lives on its own branch (18-latest active, 17-latest critical fixes only, older unsupported) and token numbers change between versions.

integration.form: static lib (libpg_query.a; shared lib target also in the Makefile)
integration.dependencies: none external at runtime besides pthreads; vendors upb (Protobuf runtime), xxHash and the extracted PostgreSQL sources; building needs make and a C compiler (nmake with Makefile.msvc on Windows)
integration.min_toolchain: not documented; C compiler with __thread thread-local storage (GCC or Clang), MSVC via Makefile.msvc
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, FreeBSD and Windows (MSVC) per the build files; x86-64, ARM and PPC per the changelog
integration.thread_safety: Thread-safe through thread-local storage since 9.5-1.4.0; each thread gets its own top-level memory context, initialized on first call and freed by a pthread exit hook (or pg_query_exit); test/concurrency.c runs 50-500 threads.

gotchas: Harness note: the fast rows call the internal pg_query_raw_parse and never free result.stderr_buffer (pg_query_raw_parse strdup()s it on every call), so the raw benchmark leaks one small allocation per iteration and omits that free from the timing; the public pg_query_parse rows free it.

Each call creates and deletes a fresh memory context and, since 18.1.0, re-measures the thread's stack to set the stack-depth limit (100 kB default, up to 2 MB); deeply nested queries now return 'stack depth limit exceeded' instead of crashing, but the numbers above were taken on an unpinned HEAD clone and may predate this.

Comments are ignored when parsing but significant when scanning (18.1.0); fingerprints changed between 17 and 18 (schema ignored, alias used) unless PG_QUERY_FINGERPRINT_RANGEVAR_PG17_COMPAT is passed.

Open issues include a process abort in pg_query_deparse_protobuf on valid parse results (#330) and PL/pgSQL parse regressions in 18.0.0 (#337); the README recommends pinning a tagged release for production.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The catalogued siblings (PEGTL, lexy, re2c, PAPAGENO, Pika) are toolkits for writing your own grammar; pick libpg_query when the grammar you need is PostgreSQL's SQL itself, since it gives byte-for-byte server parity without writing or maintaining a grammar.
verified_claims_summary: In the ProxySQL/ParserSQL comparison harness (AMD Ryzen 9 5950X, Linux 6.17, GCC 13.3 at -O3, Google Benchmark for C, Criterion with sqlparser 0.52.0 for Rust), libpg_query's internal raw parse took 230-3,304 ns per statement versus sqlparser-rs's MySQL-dialect parse_sql at 412-23,411 ns (1.8x on BEGIN, 4.8-7.1x on SELECT and INSERT, derived from page data); through the public JSON API the gain is 2.0-2.7x and BEGIN is at parity. The table comes from a rival project whose own parser is the winner, the PostgreSQL-dialect sqlparser-rs rows were run but not published, and libpg_query was an unpinned HEAD clone.
status_note: Actively maintained by pganalyze (18.1.0 released 2026-09-30 with a security fix, about 1.5k stars, BSD-3-Clause plus the PostgreSQL licence) and widely embedded (DuckDB, pganalyze, Supabase's Postgres language server); copyable, but pin a tag and upgrade past GHSA-6ggm-xmc9-8ffg if you normalize untrusted input.
